DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Myelopathy secondary to spinal cord compression.

The combination of progressive gait failure, urinary incontinence, speech difficulties (dysarthria), and likely upper motor neuron signs points strongly to compression of the spinal cord at the cervical level affecting the brainstem pathways. The MRI results you confirmed as showing cervical spinal cord compression with myelopathy align perfectly with this clinical picture, ruling out primary brainstem pathology like a tumor or stroke as the primary cause. Immediate neurosurgical consultation is indicated to prevent permanent paralysis.
